subject: MAP: Re-sequence final-mile milestones & contingency probability statement
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lin <sara.lin@lumenhealth.com>; procurement@lumenhealth.com
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-21T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: MAP: Re-sequence final-mile milestones & contingency probability statement

Hi Sara / LumenHealth procurement team —

Quick note following yesterday's weekly sync: the current MAP (v1) expects a signed PO by 2026-10-29 in order to meet the live window of 2026-11-19. Our intake team flagged a downstream approval item that looks likely to slip the PO date outside that window.

I attached a cleaned MAP_v2 and a preliminary risk register (see attachments) that lay out two options:
- Option A: Keep milestone order, accept a delivery stretch (risk: larger scope of final acceptance testing).
- Option B: Re-sequence final-mile tasks (run integration staging earlier, shift acceptance window) to preserve a partial go-live for the most critical endpoints while procurement completes.

Practical ask: can procurement confirm an updated PO ETA by end of day Thursday so we can lock a path? If PO is > 10 business days after 10/29, we recommend Option B + a 5-business-day formal rebaseline of the MAP.

I've called out probabilities (low/medium/high) for each risk in the register and included a short operational checklist for a temporary canary (canary-checklist.md). If you prefer, we can schedule a 20-min working session today to walk the MAP_v2 changes.

Attachments: 20261021_MAP_v2.pdf (redlines + milestone table), 20261021_risk_register.xlsx (probability x impact scoring), canary-checklist.md (ops playbook stub).

Thanks — appreciate a quick confirmation.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Sara Lin <sara.lin@lumenhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@lumenhealth.com; Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-21T11:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: Re-sequence final-mile milestones & contingency probability statement

Marissa —

Thanks for the heads up. Short answer: procurement's timeline changed because the legal approval for our new data residency clause hit an additional internal review step. Current best ETA for PO sign is 2026-11-08. I know that pushes things beyond your preferred window.

Can you summarize the customer-visible impact for Option B (what features are live and what's deferred)? Also, any incremental cost if we go with a temporary reserved capacity for staging while we finish approvals?

—Sara
Sara Lin
Director, Vendor Operations | LumenHealth
sara.lin@lumenhealth.com
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sara Lin <sara.lin@lumenhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-21T12:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: Re-sequence final-mile milestones & contingency probability statement

Sara / team —

Appreciate the update, Sara. Quick operational read: Option B (resequencing) minimizes user-facing risk if we move non-blocking acceptance tasks (final load testing, full dataset regression) to after a partial go-live that covers API endpoints A, B and C. Estimated items:

- Canary plan: deploy a dedicated small pool for 2 weeks to validate key paths (canary-checklist.md attached in thread).
- Cost delta (temporary pool + extra monitoring): ~USD 6.5k for the two-week window. If Lumen prefers, we can limit the canary to a single region to reduce cost (est. USD 3.2k).
- Risk scoring from register (high-probability / medium-impact): delay to non-core acceptance; low-probability / high-impact: compliance regression if the residency clause handling is incomplete.

Proposed resequence (high-level):
1) Integration staging & canary validation — 2026-11-01 to 2026-11-12
2) Partial go-live (API A/B/C only) — 2026-11-15
3) Full acceptance window start — 2026-11-29 (contingent on PO cleared)

If Lumen approves Option B, we'll update the MAP_v2 milestone table and publish a short runbook for CS/Eng.

On a process note: we should capture this as a formal 5-business-day rebaseline (documented change request) so downstream owners have a single source of truth for the new dates.

Thanks,
Grace
Grace O'Connor
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Lin <sara.lin@lumenhealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-21T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: Re-sequence final-mile milestones & contingency probability statement

All —

Agree with Grace's approach. ACTIONS:
- Approve Option B (resequence + 5-business-day formal rebaseline) to preserve a partial go-live on 2026-11-15.
- Marissa: publish MAP_v2 as the canonical MAP in HubSpot and tag the change request (DL-2026-1189-CR1).
- Priya: if procurement confirms PO on 11/08, please record acceptance and notify engineering immediately; if the PO is later than 11/08, trigger the standard escalation to Sales Leadership.
- Engineering / Solutions (cc for awareness): prepare the canary pool and enable the observability hooks in console; follow canary-checklist.md.

Sara — thanks for the quick timeline. Marissa and I will update the risk register and send a one-page executive note for Lumen's procurement leadership.
